title: 3-month token burn remediation & contractor-led surge plan (prototype)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, actionable 3-month plan to materially reduce token burn, extend runway, and preserve throughput for high-value customers by combining: a short contractor-led capacity surge (6–10 weeks), temporary negotiated pricing tiers for heavy customers, and a credits-redistribution program to prioritize essential traffic. This doc is a prototype for the exec review on 2026-03-16.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Immediate objective: cut net hosted token spend by ~30% over Q2 without degrading SLA for top 25 customers.
- Mechanism: reallocate budget across transient contractors (rapid capacity ops), negotiate interim price tiers/credits with 8 largest customers, and apply automated prefix caching to heavy sessions.
- Expected impact: runway extension of ~3–4 months at current burn rate or 18% reduction in gross headcount hiring pressure.
- Ask: approve $1.2M short-term surge budget + authority to pilot 3 pricing exceptions.

Key assumptions (inputs):
- Current blended cost per 1k tokens served: $0.023 (hosted fleet).
- Top 25 customers account for 62% of tokens but 78% of revenue.
- Contingent contractor ops rate (incl. infra, onboarding, tooling) estimated at $950/day/person.
- Contractor ramp: 2 weeks to be fully productive for ops tasks; 6–10 week engagement window.
- Negotiate up to 25% temporary surcharge / 12-month credits in exchange for committed credits.

Scenario sketches (3 scenarios):
1) Base (no action): Q2 burn continues — runway reduces by 2.8 months.
2) Remediation-lite (pricing + caching): Customer-surge credits + auto-caching yields 18–22% token-cost reduction.
3) Remediation-plus (contractor surge + pricing + caching): Target 28–35% reduction, minimal SLA impact.

Short spreadsheet summary (per-month averages):
- Current monthly token spend (hosted) ~ $4,200,000
- Target after plan (remediation-plus) ~ $2,940,000
- Contractor surge cost (one-off over 2 months) ~ $600,000
- Customer concessions (credits issued, net) ~ $240,000 impact
- Net monthly savings (after contractor amortization) ~ $820,000 in months 2–3

Headcount / contractor plan (operational sketch):
- Roles: 4 contractor infra/ops engineers (capacity tuning, autoscaling runs), 1 contractor billing analyst (customer negotiations support), 1 contractor SRE (runbook automation).
- Total FTE-equivalent: 6 contractors for 8 weeks. Estimated all-in: $600K.
- Hiring freeze: defer 3 mid-level infra hires scheduled in Q2 to preserve full-time headcount runway.

Pricing sensitivity actions (customer-level playbook):
- Tier A (top 8 customers): Offer convertible credits: immediate 10–20% up-front credits in exchange for 6–12 month committed minimums OR temporary +10–25% surcharge for overages with guaranteed latency SLO. Use legal-approved template.
- Tier B (next 17 customers): Apply soft throttles and offer cache-friendly session guidance + 5% bill credit for joint-effort prompt engineering.
- Negotiation guardrails: no permanent list-price reductions; credits must be recouped via committed revenue or documented ROI.

Operational levers (quick wins):
- Auto-prefix caching: enable strict prefix-KV caching for streaming sessions older than 15s idle. Estimated immediate savings 6–9%.
- Aggressive batching during non-peak windows: shift select long-form batch jobs to burst-reserved nodes.
- Apply model-variant routing: route low-criticality traffic to lower-cost quantized variants.

Risk and mitigation matrix (short):
- Customer churn risk (Tier A): Mitigate via executive outreach + one-week SLA credits.
- Performance regression: Pre-deploy A/B eval set on canary region for 72 hours before global roll.
- Compliance/billing confusion: billing analyst to produce per-customer impact memos prior to changes.

Decision points & timeline (three-month cadence):
- Week 0 (approval): Approve $1.2M surge envelope + negotiation authority for product and legal.
- Week 1–2: Contractor onboarding, choose 8 customers for Tier A pilot, enable autoscaling policies and caching flags in canary.
- Week 3–4: Begin Tier A negotiations; roll caching to 10% of traffic; assess early telemetry.
- Week 5–8: Full contractor ops cadence, pricing pilots, iterative tuning.
- Week 9–12: Measure net burn reduction; decide whether to convert contractors to short-term full-time hires or close engagements.

Metrics & dashboards to watch (daily/weekly):
- Net hosted token spend (daily, 7d MA)
- Top-25 customer token share and delta from baseline
- Latency P95 and P99 for Tier A customer sessions
- Credits issued vs. recovered committed revenue
- Contractor ramp velocity & runbook automation completion percentage

Open questions / unresolved items: (notes-to-self)
- Exact legal language for convertible credits — need quick template from Legal (priority).
- Which product metrics can be surfaced to customers to justify caching behavior changes? (eng-runbook)
- Accounting treatment for short contractor costs vs. capitalized onboarding? (finance).

Approvals & asks:
- Approve pilot budget: $1.2M (contractors $600k, negotiation/credits buffer $300k, ops buffer $300k).
- Approve temporary hiring freeze for 3 mid-level infra hires (Q2).
- Grant Product + Legal authority to finalize 3 Tier A customer deals under guardrails.

Next steps (immediate owners):
- Aisha: finalize budget memo for CFO + schedule 30m exec sync (by 2026-03-17).
- Daniel Kim: prepare canary deploy plan for caching and routing toggles (by 2026-03-12).
- Marta Gómez: draft customer negotiation template and short FAQ for CS (by 2026-03-13).
- Priya Nair: estimate billing/AR accounting impacts and draft memo (by 2026-03-14).

Appendix (quick model sensitivity):
- Sensitivity table (monthly net savings):
  * -10% contractor effectiveness => savings fall to ~18% (vs target 30%).
  * +10% customer acceptance of credits => net savings improve by ~4 percentage points.
  * 7-day delay in contractor onboarding => 6% slippage in month-1 savings.

Notes: This is intentionally compact. If execs like the prototype we will expand into a full sheet with month-by-month cashflow, per-customer P&L, and legal templates. For now the priority is speed: reduce burn without damaging our relationship with revenue-critical partners.
